title: Know How Cyble Brand Intelligence Can Help Stop ClickFix Campaigns in its Tracks
content_md: Booking.com's systems were never breached. Its name was. Storm-1865 spent months borrowing Booking.com's identity to get into hotel computers, and every step of that borrowing left traces on the open internet. The open internet is exactly where Cyble Brand Intelligence & Protection works. Walk through the campaign one step at a time, and at each step there is a point where it could have spotted the attacker, cut the attack short or limited the damage. What happened From December 2024, a group Microsoft tracks as Storm-1865 posed as Booking.com to target hotel and hospitality staff across North America, Europe, Oceania and South and Southeast Asia. Microsoft Threat Intelligence published its findings on March 13, 2025, and said the campaign was still running as of February 2025. The attack had four moving parts: The lure. Emails styled as Booking.com messages about negative guest reviews, guest enquiries, promotion offers or account verification. The landing page. A link, sometimes inside a PDF, opened a fake CAPTCHA laid over a faint copy of a real Booking.com page. The trick.
